name: The Agent Economy gaps
description: Dated notes on what primary pages document, and what those pages do not document, for settlement asset, spend controls, revocation, protocol composition, license, governance body, and cross-company use. Not documented uses the day the page was read. Omitted means the note has no checked source for that dimension. Rows are alphabetical by listing name.
attribution: The Agent Economy gaps (https://theagenteconomy.si/data/gaps.json), licensed under CC BY 4.0.

legend.Documented: A cited page states the fact.
legend.Not documented: The cited page does not state the fact. The line includes the day that page was read.
legend.Mixed: The note has both a documented claim and a not documented claim.
legend.Omitted: This note has no checked source for that dimension.

documented.text: Customers must approve agent purchases by default, and Walmart may require more approvals even within a spending limit. Agent Profiles, announced 21 October 2026 for the following month, let the customer approve every purchase or set a spending limit. The release gives $50, $100, and $200 as examples. Agents cannot add or change payment methods.

documented.text: The customer can delete an Agent Profile at any time. Walmart blocks agents that break its terms.

documented.text: Tools can carry readOnlyHint, untrustedContentHint, and consequentialHint. consequentialHint marks a consequential, real world or non reversible action such as transferring money, and is a signal clients can use to require user confirmation. The spec says a malicious site can omit or misrepresent hints.

documented.text: The Cloudflare blog says an edge implementation, launched in beta in August, injects a script so a site's tools become available and proxies a backend MCP server's tools to the browser. Commerce.com turned it on across almost 100,000 storefront domains, with a per merchant opt out. The shopper still clicks checkout.

documented.text: The x402.org FAQ says stablecoin payments are the primary use case, and that the protocol is extensible to traditional payment methods.
The same FAQ says x402 supports EVM compatible chains, Solana, and more.
The Linux Foundation announcement says payment types range from traditional cards to stablecoins.
documented.source_title: Linux Foundation announcement of the x402 Foundation, 14 July 2026

documented.text: The A2A x402 extension v0.2 spec defines an A2A extension for x402 payments, including an embedded flow inside AP2.
AP2's site links a human not present sample that uses x402.
The MPP documentation index includes a guide for using MPP with x402.
Mastercard's 2026-10-20 article says Agent Pay for Machines builds on x402.
